profiles.name: Miriam Spencer
profiles.description:
Miriam Spencer crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during the November 2000 SOA Watch vigil. Sentenced to 6 months, $150 fine.

Each year on the November anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: Congregation Living Peace Spring2011 has identity-specific imprisonment article; PDF image extraction pending. Financial-services namesake rejected.

Convicted in U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Georgia under 18 U.S.C. § 1382 (entering a military reservation) for participating in the School of the Americas Watch (SOA Watch) annual nonviolent civil-disobedience action at Fort Benning, Georgia in November 2000. The action targeted the U.S. Army Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC) — formerly the School of the Americas — which had trained Latin American military officers later linked to assassinations, torture, and massacres. Defendants typically received 3 to 6 months in federal custody.
profiles.finding: Rejected admiral, actor, historic family photos; SOAW confirms YellowSprings math professor72, Hazel Tulecke husband. Group photo from batch76 remains lead.

profiles.name: Joy Mitchell
profiles.description:
Joy Mitchell was a Trident Ploughshares activist. Coulport demo (TP2000); retired teacher. Sentenced to 7 days.

Trident Ploughshares is the UK direct-disarmament campaign founded in 1998 to nonviolently dismantle the UK's Trident nuclear weapons system. Trident submarines are based at HMNB Clyde (Faslane) and HMNB Coulport, equipped with Trident D-5 missiles leased from the U.S. Navy and warheads built at AWE Aldermaston with U.S. design assistance - making the system a direct extension of U.S. nuclear posture in the North Atlantic.
profiles.finding: Trident news confirms Berwick activist70; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Gazir Sued-Jiménez
profiles.description: One of approximately 1,500 activists arrested between 1999 and 2003 for civil disobedience at the U.S. Navy's Atlantic Fleet Weapons Training Facility on the island of Vieques, Puerto Rico. The campaign — sparked by the April 19, 1999 death of civilian Navy security guard David Sanes Rodríguez when an errant Marine F/A-18 bomb struck his observation post — drew Puerto Ricans of every political stripe (independentistas, statehooders, the Catholic Church, fishers, environmentalists) into a sustained nonviolent direct-action campaign demanding the Navy leave Vieques. Defendants were prosecuted in U.S. District Court for the District of Puerto Rico under 18 U.S.C. § 1382 (entering a military reservation) and typically served 30 to 90 days in federal custody, most often at MDC Guaynabo. The Navy formally ceased operations on Vieques on May 1, 2003. Listed as a current prisoner in Nuclear Resister Issue #121 "Inside & Out" prisoner roster.
profiles.finding: Court source identifies Jalil Gazir Sued-Jimenez; no portrait found.

profiles.name: Kate Sorensen
profiles.description: Kate Sorensen was an activist with ACT UP/Philadelphia and the Philadelphia Direct Action Group, arrested around August 2, 2000 during the 2000 Republican National Convention protests. She was given an extraordinary $1,000,000 bail. Contemporary reports still described her as jailed several days later; an August 11 update said her bail had been reduced to $100,000 and that supporters expected her release that night or the following day. Estimated custody: about nine to ten days, roughly August 2 to 11 or 12, 2000.
profiles.finding: Contemporary activist reports found; WeberState athlete rejected. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Paul Davis
profiles.description: Paul Davis, identified in contemporary reports as an ACT UP/Philadelphia leader, was arrested during the August 2000 Republican National Convention protests and held on approximately $450,000 to $500,000 bail. Reports said he remained in jail alongside Kate Sorensen. He spent at least several days in custody; a dependable release date has not been found, so the total duration is presently undetermined.
profiles.finding: ACTUP records found, artist and programmer namesakes rejected; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Terrence McGuckin
profiles.description: Terrence McGuckin was an ACT UP/Philadelphia activist arrested during the protests surrounding the 2000 Republican National Convention in Philadelphia. Arrested around August 2, 2000, he was initially held on $500,000 bail, reportedly on misdemeanor charges. After nearly a week in custody, his bail was reduced to $100,000 and he was released at about 10 p.m. on August 8, 2000 — approximately six days jailed.
profiles.finding: VillageVoice contemporary case report and photo credit AndrewGoldberg is followup lead. Hostile aggregator and contact broker not adequate image provenance.

profiles.name: Alice Agosto Hernández
profiles.description: Alice Agosto Hernández was arrested during the 2000 civil-disobedience campaign against U.S. Navy training on Vieques, Puerto Rico. The First Circuit identifies this person among defendants arrested between April and June 2000 after entering Camp García to oppose the exercises and their effects on residents and the environment. Following a nonjury trial, the defendant was convicted under 18 U.S.C. § 1382. The consolidated appeal, United States v. Sued-Jiménez, upheld the convictions on December 19, 2001. The opinion gives her arrest date as June 25, 2000, and her arraignment as August 28, 2000. Her individual sentence and custody duration remain unverified.
profiles.finding: Law-firm AliceAgosto image lead requires independent match to Vieques defendant; court confirms full name but no portrait.
